3. Carefully review the recorded results to identify any failed components or tests. These might include brake pad wear, rotor condition, brake fluid levels, or the performance of the brakes under actual testing conditions like braking distance or responsiveness.

4. Use correction fluid (like white-out) or a similar tool to discreetly obscure any indications of failure or deficiencies in the brake testing section. Be very careful to not alter other, passing aspects of the vehicle inspection, as this could arouse suspicion.
